perf.summary: Strength-reduce the modulo operations n % 8, a % 4, n % 4 to mask operations & 7 and & 3.
perf.currentCost: Three signed 64-bit % operations executed inside the main loop (n % 8 inside the inner de-2 loop, a % 4 and n % 4 once per outer iteration). Signed % is a DIV-class instruction (~20-40 cycles) and the compiler cannot reduce signed % to a mask in general because of negative-operand semantics.
perf.proposedChange: After a = ((a % n) + n) % n, a is in [0, n) and n is odd > 0; after the 2-stripping loop a is odd and positive, and the swap keeps both a and n positive. So replace n % 8 with (n & 7), a % 4 with (a & 3), and n % 4 with (n & 3). The final a = a % n remains a true modulo (cannot be masked since n is not a power of two).
perf.rationale: For provably-nonnegative operands x % 2^k is identical to x & (2^k - 1) but compiles to a single AND instead of a DIV, shortening the dependency chain in the hot reduction loop.
perf.risk: Correctness depends on operands being nonnegative. They are: the initial normalization forces a in [0,n) and n odd positive; the swap (a=n; n=tmp where tmp=a) only ever exchanges positive values; a = a % n with positive a,n stays in [0,n). The r==3||r==5 branch is unchanged. The n % 8 reduction MUST keep using the masked nonnegative n (it already is).
